body:
arm64 simulator does build now, so this may not need removing.

The blocks in godot-build-scripts build-ios/build.sh were commented out in 2021 over cctools-port and the LLVM of the time. Dockerfile.apple has neither now, it is swiftly's clang plus the Xcode SDKs. iOS templates are a static archive, so ld64 isn't in the picture for this target either.

On an Apple Silicon Mac against master 9ba32b09e0:

```
scons platform=ios arch=arm64 ios_simulator=yes target=template_debug

$ otool -l main.ios.template_debug.arm64.simulator.o | grep -A4 LC_BUILD_VERSION
      cmd LC_BUILD_VERSION
  cmdsize 24
 platform 7
    minos 15.0
      sdk 26.5

$ lipo -info libgodot.ios.debug.simulator.a    # arm64 and x86_64 lipo'd together
Architectures in the fat file: libgodot.ios.debug.simulator.a are: x86_64 arm64
```

platform 7 is IOSSIMULATOR. Built into a project exported with the official 4.8.dev3 template it runs on an arm64 iPhone 17 simulator, where the shipped template fails at link with `found architecture 'x86_64', required architecture 'arm64'`.

godotengine/godot-build-scripts#169 has the change, four lines uncommented and the two simulator archives lipo'd instead of only the x86_64 one being copied. The caveat is that I verified with Xcode's clang, not inside godot-apple, since I have no podman here. If someone can run it in the container that would settle it either way.

> arm64 simulator does build now, so this may not need removing.

Both arm64 and x86_64 simulator libs are buildable (and always were buildable on macOS), there were issues with cross building, but updated build system should not have any issues with it.

The reason for removal is limited Metal support in simulator (bunch of missing features used by the engine), which make simulator almost useless (it is still being evaluated whether it is worth working around these limitations and keeping simulator or not).
